newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FRANCOPHONE COMMUNITY MINISTER GRAFE RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: FRANCOPHONE COMMUNITY MINISTER GRAFE RESIGNS.

text.p: Jean-Pierre Grafe, a minister in Belgium's Francophone regional government who has been accused of having under-aged sex, said on Monday he was resigning, Belga news agency reported.
Grafe was accused along with the Federal Government's Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo of having sex with children under the country's legal age of consent of 16 years.

Both men have denied the charges, and earlier on Monday the country's top court, the Cour de Cassation, handed a report to a special parliamentary commission looking into the Di Rupo case that said the main charges against him were baseless.
"The magnitude of the rumours concerning me oblige me, firstly, to proclaim loudly my innocence," Grafe said in a statement to Belga.
"It is necessary to make a choice, painful but necessary. Politics is also a matter of taking the necessary decisions in all clarity.
"I have therefore asked to be freed from my community and regional ministerial functions. The current climate does not allow me to exercise them fully and with the same authority," Grafe said.
"I will be able then...while pursuing my parliamentary functions, to organise my defence and gather the elements necessary to prove my innocence," he said.
The Cour de Cassation is due on Tuesday to hand a report on its investigations into the allegations against Grafe to the francophone regional government.
